## Plan document present and linked

The required plan exists at [dev/active/2d109173-plan.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/dev/active/2d109173-plan.md:1), is substantive, and is linked as a `design` document in `issue.documents`. The supporting investigation is also linked and complete.

## Completeness against the criteria

All six `[hard]` criteria are addressed in the criteria table and mapped to executable tasks in the coverage map at [dev/active/2d109173-plan.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/dev/active/2d109173-plan.md:398).

The six Group-B footprints cover the complete amended in-scope surface, including `docs/index.md` and `docs/README.md`. REQ-05 explicitly adds homes for `serve` and `events` at lines 310–319. REQ-06 now requires every area to record missing projection surfaces and feeds those records into a downstream follow-up task at lines 377–396.

## Technical soundness and architectural fit

The plan correctly uses the project’s existing sources of truth and extension points:

- `jit --schema` with direct Clap-definition fallback for its known omissions.
- Existing addressable-item and projection mechanisms.
- Exec-gate conventions in `.jit/gates.toml`.
- The existing context flow through `scripts/ai-review.sh`.
- Source-level handling for the defective generated `State` enumeration.

The treatment of `TESTING.md` is now consistent with the container’s amended authoritative scope: it is explicitly classified as contributor documentation and relocated to `dev/TESTING.md`. The current omission from [scripts/doc-review-prompt.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/scripts/doc-review-prompt.md:9) is therefore intentional rather than an exhaustive-review gap.

## Decomposition and dependencies

The decomposition is coherent and substantially implementation-ready:

- Both enablers precede every area audit.
- Area footprints are disjoint apart from explicitly governed link-repointing edits.
- The oversized reference area is split cleanly.
- Every audit has a shared, concrete acceptance template.
- The Group-C follow-up task depends on all six audits, so it cannot close before all newly discovered projection gaps are available.

The plan also identifies the limited cross-footprint collision around relocation edits and calls for serialization where necessary at lines 424–425.

## Risks and actionability

Material risks are identified with credible mitigations: stale binaries, reviewer sampling, checker confidence, cross-area contradictions, relocation collisions, schema defects, and task sizing.

Commands, expected outputs, source fallbacks, task footprints, seeded defects, acceptance criteria, and blast radii are sufficiently specific for implementation without re-deriving the design.

## Prior review feedback

Both previous blocking findings are resolved:

- The `TESTING.md` review-surface mismatch was retired through an explicit owner-approved scope change reflected in the container description and plan decision D7.
- REQ-06 follow-up filing now has defined inputs from every area audit and is ordered downstream of all six audits at lines 377–396.
